feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. The candidate keeps the iteration 5 geometry, base_speed 1.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.1, sensor weights and search_right, and lowers kp from 2.0 to 1.6. Iteration 5 (kp 2.0) is the best raced design at 75.779. Against iteration 4 (kp 2.5, otherwise identical), progress rose on every track: oval 0.21 to 0.29, s-bend 0.126 to 0.153, slalom 0.084 to 0.108. Every run still ended off track with one line-loss event, and max_error stayed at about 0.063 to 0.067 m, above the 0.06 m limit. Oscillation stayed low (0.14 to 0.16), so the failure is a drift to an edge, not weaving. This is a clean single-variable step along the kp trend, and the candidate is valid and not obviously broken. Approve it so the race can confirm or reject the trend. Read the result this way. (1) If progress rises again on the oval, s-bend and slalom, and line_loss_events does not rise, keep kp near 1.6 and test the sensor geometry next (sensor_size 0.016 at the same x positions). (2) If progress falls, or line_loss_events rises, revert to kp 2.0 (the best raced design) and test the sensor geometry from there. (3) If max_error stays near 0.063 m on every track whatever kp does, proportional gain is not the limiter, and the next lever is the sensor span or sensor_size, not more gain changes.
requested_changes: Race as written. If progress rises on all three tracks with no added line-loss events, keep kp 1.6 and change only sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 (same x positions), since kp 2.5 to 2.0 to 1.6 has moved progress monotonically.

If progress falls or line_loss_events rises at kp 1.6, revert kp to 2.0 (iteration 5, 75.779) and change only sensor_size to 0.016 at the same x positions, to test whether the edge is reached because the outer sensors lose the tape too early.

If max_error stays near 0.063 m on every track whatever kp does, stop tuning gains and test the sensor span (outer sensors at x = plus or minus 0.05 m, with the 12 mm footprint or the 16 mm footprint).
